## What changed

**`proxy test` reported a clean chain while `apt-get update` through the same
proxy was failing.** Both were telling the truth about different things: the
apt rung ran `apt-cache madison`, which reads the lists already on disk and
says nothing whatsoever about the network. On a real machine it answered
"versions: 591" one second before the climb died on
`E: The repository … no longer has a Release file`.

The probe now refreshes the GitLab repository for real — through the same
proxy configuration the upgrade uses — into a throwaway lists directory with
its own sources file, so a diagnostic stays a diagnostic and the system lists
are untouched. `madison` is still reported, because "the lists on disk are
usable" is worth knowing; it is simply no longer mistaken for "the repository
is reachable".

Signature verification is not disabled for the probe. A failure to verify gets
its own verdict instead: the route works, the key does not, and those are fixed
in different places. Sending someone to reconfigure a working proxy because apt
could not check a signature is worse than saying nothing.
